verses.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
Those who are wise shall shine as the brightness of the expanse; and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars forever and ever.
But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run back and forth, and knowledge shall be increased.”
Then I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two others stood, one on the river bank on this side, and the other on the river bank on that side.
One said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?

I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives forever that it shall be for a time, times, and a half; and when they have finished breaking in pieces the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.
I heard, but I didn’t understand: then I said, my lord, what shall be the issue of these things?
He said, Go your way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.
Many shall purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined; but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand; but those who are wise shall understand.
From the time that the continual burnt offering shall be taken away, and the abomination that makes desolate set up, there shall be one thousand two hundred ninety days.
Blessed is he who waits, and comes to the one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
But go you your way until the end; for you shall rest, and shall stand in your lot, at the end of the days.

footnotes.content: Michael stands for God's people—a guardian so strong the enemy trembles before him. In our darkest hour, when trouble seems endless, the Lord never leaves His own without a defender. Notice: deliverance isn't by chance, but written in a book, secured by a hand you can trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sleeping in dust, yet awaking—what tenderness in that image. The resurrection separates the faithful from those who turned away. I've learned that choices made now echo in eternity, not as fate, but as the natural fruit of hearts turned toward Jesus or away from Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wise shine like heaven itself; those who draw others to righteousness shine like the stars. A life spent pointing others toward Jesus doesn't disappear—it becomes part of the brightness that fills eternity. That's the sweetest kind of legacy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Daniel is told to seal these visions until the end of days—yet here they sit, open in your hands. The very knowledge that was sealed is now revealed. The Lord's timing works in ways that surprise us, moving from mystery to clarity as His Kingdom unfolds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In a vision, Daniel stands between two heavenly figures at the river's edge, watching. There's comfort in witnessing—the truth is never left to one prophet alone. God surrounds His word with testimony: angels gather, voices speak, so we know we're not hearing an echo, but reality.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "How long?" The question echoes through centuries. We ask it in grief, in exile, in waiting. The one clothed in linen—standing above the waters—is patient with the question. The Lord is not annoyed by our "how long?" He answers with precision and grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An oath sworn by the Eternal One: a time, times, and a half. The answer comes—specific, measured, bounded. Trouble will break the power of God's people, yes, but notice: it has an end. The Lord doesn't just comfort; He sets limits on what His enemies can do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Daniel heard but didn't understand—and he said so honestly. There's no shame in that gap between hearing and comprehending. Even a faithful, praying soul stands sometimes in mystery. What matters is the asking, the reaching toward understanding rather than pretending you already have it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end." Not forgotten—sealed. There's a difference. Some mysteries the Lord keeps close, not to hide from us, but because we're not yet ready to carry them. Trust that His silence has wisdom in it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The righteous purify themselves; the wicked do wickedly. Each follows their own path, and neither understands the other. It's a quiet truth: refinement and wisdom aren't natural; they come through surrender. The wise choose to be refined, and in that choosing, they come to understand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A number of days—1,290—marks the interval from desolation to restoration. Whether literal or symbolic, the message is clear: there is a timeline. Evil and desecration don't reign forever. The God who counts days also ends them, and brings His people home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Blessed is he who waits." Not just survives, but waits—holds on, keeps faith, holds steady until the one thousand three hundred thirty-five days. Waiting is an act of belief. To wait is to say: I trust He's coming, and it will be worth it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Go your way until the end; you shall rest, and stand in your lot." Readers today hear an echo of Jesus' words to His own: rest from your labors, and enter into joy. The lot assigned to you is safe, preserved, and waiting. As of 2026-10, that promise still holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
